look_here_first: Small annual amaranth with mostly axillary congested flower clusters rather than a big terminal spike, and relatively small ovate-to-rhombic leaves.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local + 1 wild iNaturalist observation; Kew accepts species native in Texas and the southeastern/south-central U.S.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning; only current native-range evidence should feed native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The lack of a big terminal panicle is the fast cue. Smaller and more cluster-forming than Palmer, redroot, or green amaranth.
